The Claim Petition For Compensation And Seeking
Enhancement Of Compensation.

This Appeal, Coming On For Further Orders, This
Day, Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice N S Sanjay Gowda
 Oral Judgment
1.
The claimant is in appeal being dissatisfied with a sum of Rs.2,61,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The occurrence of the accident and the liability of the insurer to pay the compensation is not in dispute.
3. The Tribunal on assessing the medical evidence has come to the conclusion that the claimant had suffered a disability of 14% to the whole body.
In my view, this assessment of the Tribunal cannot be found fault with.

4. However, the Tribunal has taken the notional income of the claimant as Rs.5,000/- per month,
since there was no evidence to that effect.

As the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority has determined the NC: 2024:KHC:50874 notional income as Rs.9,000/- for the accident of the year 2015 , it would be appropriate to determine the notional income of the claimant at Rs.9,000/-.

5. Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.2,26,800/- (Rs.9,000/- X 12 X 15 X 14%) towards 'loss of future earnings'.
6.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.55,000/-
towards 'pain and suffering' and Rs.45,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.

In my view, it would be appropriate to enhance the said sums to Rs.75,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' and Rs.70,000/-
towards 'loss of amenities'.

S.S.Ravi @ Rajappa vs Asgar Ali, S/O Ahamad Pasha on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141651809/
2 7.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/-
towards 'medical expenses', since it is based on the documentary evidence, it is hence affirmed.

8. The Tribunal has taken the laid up period as three months and has awarded a sum of Rs.15,000/-
towards 'loss of income during laid up period'.

In my NC: 2024:KHC:50874 view, since the notional income is now taken as Rs.9,000/-, it would be appropriate award a sum of Rs.27,000/-
(Rs.9,000/- X 3 months) towards 'loss of income during laid up period'.
9.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/-
towards 'conveyance, attendant, food, nourishment charges'.
In my view, since the claimant was hospitalized for 41 days, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards the said sum.

10. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:

1.

2. Pain and suffering 55,000/- 75,000/-
3. Loss of amenities 45,000/- 70,000/-
Loss of income 15,000/- 27,000/-
4.
during the laid up Loss of future 1,26,000/- 2,26,800/-
5. earnings Conveyance, 10,000/- 20,000/-

6 .

nourishment charges S.S.Ravi @ Rajappa vs Asgar Ali, S/O Ahamad Pasha on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141651809/
3  Total 2,61,000/- 4,28,800/-
11.

Accordingly, the claimant is held entitled for  compensation of Rs.4,28,800/- as against Rs.2,61,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation.
12.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
13. This appeal is, accordingly, allowed in part.
